sentence_of_record: PROFILE-R-FILTERED: on the merged board (21,536 verdicts, 2,811 judged q) the answer-disagreement filter keeps 12,614 matches (conv A, missing kept; 10,442 conv B) on 2,511 / 2,399 questions; the judge-built anchor profile's split-half R falls from 0.7183 [0.6076, 0.8291] to 0.5613 [0.3385, 0.7842] (conv A; 0.4477 [0.2183, 0.6772] conv B): P1 FAILED, falsifier (< 0.60) FIRES, registrar's addition FAILED at the point, P2 HELD (Psychology, Other, Business PWI -> FAIL), P3 HELD (Philosophy 114, Health 116, History 100 UNDETERMINED-by-support). The drop decomposes into support (a random subsample of the same match count per anchor reads 0.627, 58% of the drop) and selection (0.627 -> 0.561): the dropped same-answer matches carry a reproducible order of their own (AGREE-only R 0.648 vs 0.46-0.50 random; ~0 under permutation) anti-correlated with the key profile (two-way r -0.18), and the filtered profile tracks the key profile better (r 0.54 vs 0.28). [CORRECTED 2026-09-19 by AGREE-ORDER (D3; docs/reviews/2026-09-19_zero_call_batch2.md, 83cb8e5): "anti-correlated with the key profile (two-way r -0.18)" is a two-way (model x anchor) interaction correlation between the AGREE per-anchor theta table and the key table; the AGREE-only order itself tracks the key at 0.926 and the unfiltered theta at 0.976 (Spearman over the 20 models), and its deviation profile correlates +0.40 two-way with the length profile; "the dropped pairs carry a non-key order" reads: they carry the board's order with a non-key, length-tracking deviation profile. Whether that order's reproducibility (R 0.648) is length is UNDETERMINED (AGREE-ORDER).] The key-20 row's 0.9139 -> 0.8618 on the filtered questions is question selection (random-q 0.904), not the same mechanism. Consequence as registered: the newcomer profile-coverage bill is not halved by the filter; at half density the profile fails 0.70 with or without it. plain_description.what: On about 21,500 existing verdicts, the test kept only matches where the two models gave different final answers. This filter roughly halves the judging bill for a new model. It then measured how reproducible the per-subject model order stays, by comparing two random halves of the data.
plain_description.why: It checks whether the cheaper evaluation still gives a reliable per-subject profile of the models.
plain_description.information: If reliability held, new models could be profiled at about half the cost. If it dropped, the saving costs precision. Result: done. Reliability fell from 0.72 to 0.56, below the 0.60 bar, so the prediction failed. About 58% of the drop is just from having fewer matches. The rest is because the dropped same-answer matches carry an order of their own. The filtered profile actually tracks the answer key better. This does not show that the filter 'destroys' the profile. Older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
